fact.text: Pioneer 10's nuclear power generators were designed to last at least two years. They kept working for more than thirty.

heads_up: „airBaltic“ atsisako skrydžių maršrutu Vilnius–Diuseldorfas dėl prastų finansinių rezultatų.
Šildymo kompensacijų gali kreiptis ne tik mažiausias pajamas gaunantys gyventojai.

lithuania.headline: EK neskyrė Baltijos šalims 500 mln. eurų gynybai nuo dronų
lithuania.summary: Europos Komisija atmetė Baltijos šalių prašymą skirti papildomų 500 mln. eurų antidroninei gynybai ir pasiūlė lengvatines SAFE paskolas – Lietuvai jų prieinama beveik 6,4 mlrd. eurų. Ministras Robertas Kaunas tikėjosi didesnio eurokomisaro Andriaus Kubiliaus palaikymo, bet sako, kad planuojami oro gynybos pirkimai nesikeičia.
lithuania.context: Pastaraisiais metais Lietuvos oro erdvę ne kartą pažeidė dronai ir balionai iš Baltarusijos, todėl Baltijos šalys bendrai prašė ES lėšų gynybai nuo jų. Premjeras Mindaugas Sinkevičius EK sprendimą pavadino solidarumo stoka, o prezidento patarėjas sako, kad šalys tikriausiai kreipsis dar kartą.

lithuania.headline: „Čekiukų“ byloje įtarimai Margeliui ir dar 14 politikų
lithuania.summary: Specialiųjų tyrimų tarnyba pareiškė įtarimus dar 15 esamų ir buvusių tarybų narių iš Kalvarijos, Jonavos, Kaišiadorių, Lazdijų, Alytaus ir Akmenės rajonų dėl suklastotų kuro išlaidų apyskaitų. Buvęs Lazdijų meras Artūras Margelis įtariamas padaręs 1332 eurų žalą, o didžiausia – beveik 15,5 tūkst. eurų – nustatyta Jonavoje.
lithuania.context: Skandalas prasidėjo 2019 m., kai žurnalistai atskleidė, kad savivaldybių tarybų nariai veiklai skirtas lėšas apmokėdavo neatitinkančiais tikrovės čekiais ir apyskaitomis. Nuo tada įtarimai pareikšti dešimtims politikų visoje Lietuvoje.

lithuania.headline: Nausėda ir Merzas Berlyne aptarė Lietuvos saugumą
lithuania.summary: Oficialaus vizito Vokietijoje metu prezidentas Gitanas Nausėda Berlyne susitiko su kancleriu Friedrichu Merzu, prezidentu Franku-Walteriu Steinmeieriu ir Bundestago pirmininke Julia Klöckner; aptarta Europos gynyba, gynybos pramonė ir parama Ukrainai. Trečiadienį jis lankosi Diuseldorfe ir dalyvauja Lietuvos ir Vokietijos verslo forume.
lithuania.context: 2022 m. vasarą Vokietija įsipareigojo dislokuoti Lietuvoje brigadą – iš viso apie 5 tūkst. karių ir civilių. Didžioji jos dalis turi persikelti iki 2026 m., o visą operacinį pajėgumą brigada pasieks 2027 m.

world.headline: Democrats win control of both houses of Congress
world.summary: Democrats won both the Senate and the House, needing a net gain of four Senate seats and taking at least seven, including Texas, Ohio, Kansas, Maine, Iowa and both Carolinas. Trump said he would accept the results and that the Iran war and higher petrol prices played a role.
world.why: Covered by 12+ outlets, top of every front page
world.context: In November 2024 Republicans won the presidency, the Senate and the House, holding a 53-seat Senate majority. Midterms are traditionally a verdict on the president, and this one came amid the US-Israel war on Iran and rising living costs. Trump can still veto laws passed by the new Congress.

world.headline: Spain's transport minister resigns after train crash that killed 69
world.summary: Óscar Puente resigned and dropped out of Spain's 29 November election, six days after a Renfe high-speed train ploughed into a stationary Iryo train near Urda, south of Madrid, killing at least 69 people.
world.context: It was Spain's second deadly crash on the same line this year: in January, 46 people died. The opposition blamed Puente for an unsafe rail system, and the disaster weighs on Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, who trails in the polls.

world.headline: Hoax bomb threats hit seven flights across Europe
world.summary: Seven planes flying from the UK, Ireland, Denmark, Portugal and Italy were searched or diverted in Poland, Spain, Italy and Bulgaria after bomb threats; four were Ryanair flights, Italian jets escorted one into Rome, and no explosives were found.
world.context: The UK called them malicious hoaxes; investigators see no immediate sign of a hostile state but are checking whether the threats were coordinated.

world.headline: Tusk says Poland foiled possible provocation at Russian border
world.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Poland had received information about worrying activity near its border with Russia and had foiled a possible provocation.
world.context: Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Poland has faced drone incursions, sabotage and arson it blames on Moscow. Its border with Russia's Kaliningrad exclave is a key NATO frontier next to Lithuania.

interesting.headline: AMD posts record $13.4bn quarter on data centre demand
interesting.summary: AMD reported record revenue of $13.4bn, $8.5bn of it from data centres, and forecast another record of $17bn next quarter, while gaming revenue fell 40%.
interesting.context: AMD is Nvidia's main rival in AI chips; AI data-centre demand is also driving up memory prices for PCs and consoles.

interesting.headline: Google lets schools turn off AI, but only by losing Search
interesting.summary: From next year Google will switch off its AI tools for school students unless administrators turn them on, but schools that block AI also lose Google Search, because AI is built into it.

interesting.headline: Cinemark and Regal snub Netflix's 'Cliff Booth' film
interesting.summary: Cinemark and Regal won't give Imax screens to Brad Pitt's Netflix film, written by Quentin Tarantino and directed by David Fincher, over its two-week cinema window; it opens 25 November and streams from 23 December.
interesting.context: The film is a sequel to Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood and Netflix's first Imax release.

interesting.headline: Countries refuse to play ice hockey against Russia
interesting.summary: After a sports court lifted Russia's ban on 30 October, Finland, Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Latvia and the Czech Republic said they won't face Russia, and Canada's PM Mark Carney barred Russians from next month's world juniors.
interesting.context: Russia was banned from international hockey after invading Ukraine in 2022.

ongoing.title: Russia-Ukraine war
ongoing.update: Russia pounded Ukraine's power grid ahead of trilateral peace talks in Abu Dhabi next week, which the Kremlin confirmed, and Germany's Merz said he doubts Moscow wants a ceasefire. A Ukrainian drone hit an Ozon warehouse in southern Russia overnight.
ongoing.context: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 after annexing Crimea in 2014. Ukraine pushed Russian troops back from Kyiv and later retook land in the south and east, but the front has since ground into a war of attrition. US-brokered talks began in 2025 and were suspended in February.

ongoing.title: US-Iran tensions
ongoing.update: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said four oil tankers hit mines and were destroyed near the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran called the US reply to its seven conditions for reopening the strait unconvincing, while Trump called Tuesday's strike on an anti-aircraft site 'minor' and said there was no immediate plan for more.
ongoing.context: Decades of hostility over Iran's nuclear programme turned into open war in February, when the US and Israel struck Iran. Iran has since controlled the Strait of Hormuz, attacking ships that cross without its permission, which sent oil prices soaring. Qatar is mediating indirect talks on reopening it.

ongoing.title: Cyber-attacks on European supermarkets
ongoing.update: Germany, Romania and the UK reported hacked supermarket refrigeration too, bringing the total to at least 11 countries; the EU called the attacks 'not isolated' and promised a joint response, and Italy met its intelligence chiefs. A Romanian official called it semi-amateurish, not a state actor.
ongoing.context: Last month hackers raised freezer temperatures in hundreds of French supermarkets, and on Monday attacks spread to Belgium, Ireland, Sweden, the Netherlands and other countries, spoiling tonnes of food. No one has claimed responsibility.

ongoing.title: Protests across France and Europe
ongoing.update: Unions and housing groups from France, the UK, Belgium, Spain, Italy, Portugal and Greece called for coordinated cost-of-living rallies across Europe on Friday 20 November and the following weekend.
ongoing.context: Youth-led protests over living costs and poor prospects began in France this autumn, with pupils blockading high schools, and spread to other European countries. Unions have joined in with strikes.
